violations.name: Letter grade card not posted, hidden or removed
violations.law: 24 RCNY §23-07; NYC Health Code §81.51; 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, codes 20-05, 20-06, 20-07
violations.note: Appendix 23-C: code 20-06 grade card not posted $500 (default $1,000); code 20-05 card not conspicuously posted or not visible to passersby $500 (default $1,000); code 20-07 grade card removed, destroyed or defaced $1,000 (default $2,000). The game uses the removal row: $1,000, or $2,000 if the summons is ignored. Numbers read in search excerpts of the rule text; the page itself could not be opened from this session.

violations.name: Hand-wash sink blocked, without hot water, soap or paper towels
violations.law: NYC Health Code §81.21; 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, code 05D
violations.note: Appendix 23-A, code 05D (critical): no hand wash facility in or next to the toilet room or within 25 feet of food preparation, facility blocked or used for something else, no hot and cold running water, no soap or drying device: 10 points at condition IV and 28 points at condition V, which alone is a C. Appendix 23-C penalty $300 to $350. The one closure day is my estimate: with no hot water in the shop at all the inspector cannot let service continue until it is back.

violations.name: Ready-to-eat food handled with bare hands
violations.law: NYC Health Code §81.07; 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, code 04C
violations.note: Penalty schedule, code 04C, a public health hazard: food worker does not use a utensil or other barrier to avoid bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food: $250, $300, $350, $400 and $600 by condition level, the level set by the number of workers doing it. A pastry picked up without tongs, tissue or gloves counts. Game formula: $300 in the first month up to $600.

violations.name: Dogs or other live animals inside the shop
violations.law: NYC Health Code §81.25; 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, code 04O
violations.note: Penalty schedule, code 04O (critical): live animal other than fish in a tank or a service animal present in the food or non-food areas: $200, $200, $250, $300, $350 by the number of animals. Service animals must be let in; a pet dog may sit only at outdoor tables under the city's dogs-in-outdoor-dining rules.

violations.name: Refusing or obstructing a health inspection
violations.law: NYC Health Code §3.15(a); 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, code 07A
violations.note: Appendix 23-C, code 07A: obstruction of Department personnel $1,000 (seen in the rule excerpt). The $2,000 ceiling is my assumption that the default penalty doubles, as it does for the grade card rows; the default figure was not in the excerpt. Locking the door, hiding the kitchen or keeping the inspector waiting all count, and the inspection then happens anyway.

violations.name: Fire extinguishers missing, blocked or not serviced
violations.law: NYC Fire Code FC 906; 3 RCNY §109-03, Appendix A, Violation Category 1
violations.note: FDNY penalty schedule, Violation Category 1 (portable fire extinguishers and fire hoses): first violation $600, mitigated to $300 if you appear at the hearing and prove it was fixed by the hearing date, $1,000 if you default; second violation $1,500 (mitigated $750, maximum $5,000). FDNY's portable extinguisher flyer: extinguishers must be serviced yearly by a company holding an FDNY certificate (W-96) and checked visually every month, with the tag dated and initialed. Fire Code section number cited from memory.

violations.name: Exit door or exit path blocked
violations.law: NYC Fire Code FC 1031 (maintenance of means of egress); 3 RCNY §109-03, Appendix A, Violation Category 9
violations.note: FDNY penalty schedule, Violation Category 9 (rooftop access and means of egress): first violation $950, mitigated $475, $1,000 on default; second violation $2,375 (mitigated $1,185, maximum $5,000). Milk crates, cup cases and the mop bucket in the back corridor are the usual cause in a small shop. Fire Code section number cited from memory.

violations.name: Overcrowding: more people than the space is approved for
violations.law: NYC Fire Code FC 107.6; NYC Administrative Code §28-117.1 (Place of Assembly Certificate of Operation for 75 or more people); 3 RCNY §109-03, Appendix A, Violation Category 10
violations.note: FDNY penalty schedule, Violation Category 10 (overcrowding): first violation $950, mitigated $475, $1,000 on default; second violation $2,375 (mitigated $1,185, maximum $5,000). The game charges $950 the first time and caps at the second-violation amount. A room that gathers 75 or more people needs a Place of Assembly Certificate of Operation (NYC Business restaurant page); a small cafe has none, so a packed open-mic night breaks the rule. Fire Code and Administrative Code section numbers cited from memory. Fire officers can also order the room emptied on the spot.

violations.name: Candles or open flame without an FDNY permit
violations.law: NYC Fire Code FC 105.6, FC 308; 3 RCNY §109-03, Appendix A, Violation Category 3
violations.note: FDNY Restaurant Fire Safety Guide (2026 edition): open flames such as candles in a dining area need an FDNY permit; the yearly inspection fee is $210. FDNY penalty schedule, Violation Category 3 (permits): first violation $700, mitigated $350, $1,000 on default; second violation $1,750. Fire Code section numbers cited from memory.

violations.name: Construction, plumbing or electrical work without a Buildings permit
violations.law: NYC Administrative Code §28-105.1, §28-213.1 (civil penalty for work without a permit)
violations.note: Department of Buildings: for buildings other than one- and two-family homes the civil penalty for work without a permit is 21 times the permit fee, never less than $6,000 and never more than $15,000; the inspector also posts a Stop Work Order, and working through it costs $6,000 for the first offense. The work must then be legalized with filed plans, so the permit is paid for anyway. Numbers read in search excerpts of DOB pages and service notices; the section numbers are cited from memory.

violations.name: Working through a Stop Work Order
violations.criminal: Violating a Stop Work Order is also a misdemeanor under the Administrative Code (§28-207.2, cited from memory).
violations.note: Seen at the Department of Buildings Stop Work Order page: first offense $6,000. The amount for later offenses was not in the excerpt (from memory it is $12,000); the game charges $6,000 for every month the work goes on. The order stays on the door until the permit exists and the penalties are paid.

violations.name: Sidewalk and gutter not swept
violations.note: DSNY guide for businesses, Avoiding Common Sanitation Violations: failure to clean the sidewalk $100 to $300; failure to clean 18 inches from the curb into the street $100 to $300 (two separate tickets). Sanitation agents may ticket a commercial property only during two one-hour periods a day, printed on the DSNY notice for the block. Game formula: $100 the first month, up to $300.

violations.name: Shop trash in public litter baskets, no private carter
violations.law: NYC Administrative Code §16-116 (commercial waste must go to a licensed private carter), §16-120(c) and (e)
violations.note: DSNY guide for businesses: every business must hire a private carter and post its decal; business waste may never be placed in or beside the corner litter baskets; fine $100 to $300 (Administrative Code §16-120(c) and (e)). Game formula: $100 plus $100 for each further month, capped at $300 per ticket. Agents open the bags and look for mail and receipts with the shop's name. §16-116 cited from memory.

violations.name: A-frame sign or merchandise blocking the sidewalk
violations.note: NYC311: a sandwich or A-frame sign may not reach more than 3 feet into the sidewalk from the building. The Sanitation Department told the Midtown Gazette in 2015 that the fine is $100 for a first sign violation and up to $300 after that; a New York coffee shop was reported fined $300 for a sidewalk sign. I did not find the current penalty row, so the amounts are from press reports. Section numbers cited from memory.

violations.name: Backflow prevention device not tested this year
violations.note: OATH water penalty schedule: failure to submit the annual backflow test report (15 RCNY §20-04(e)) $500, mitigated to $50 if the report is filed before the first hearing date, $1,000 maximum. The device on the water service must be tested once a year by a state-certified tester and the report sent to the Department of Environmental Protection, which finds missing reports from its own records. In 2018 the city wrote 8,780 violations for missing reports (Public Advocate). The state code section is cited from memory.

violations.name: Music too loud for the neighbors
violations.law: NYC Administrative Code §24-231(a) (commercial music); 15 RCNY §47-02 (Noise Code penalty schedule)
violations.note: Noise Code: music from a commercial establishment may not exceed 42 dB(A) measured inside a neighbor's home. Penalty schedule for §24-231(a): $2,000 for a first offense, $4,000 for a second, $6,000 for a third; maximums $8,000, $16,000 and $24,000. A Department of Environmental Protection form lets a first offender bring the $2,000 down to $0 by admitting the violation and filing proof of correction from a noise consultant by the deadline. Found through 311 complaints: an inspector takes a reading in the complainant's apartment.

violations.name: Card surcharge not shown in the posted price
violations.note: General Business Law §518 as in force since February 11, 2024: a seller who adds a credit card surcharge must post the highest total price including the surcharge, and the surcharge may not be more than what the card processor charges the seller; civil penalty up to $500 per violation, enforced by local consumer agencies. A sign that says '3% fee on cards' next to a single menu price does not comply; two posted prices (cash and card) do. The rule covers credit cards, not debit cards.

officials.name: Fire inspector
officials.realProcess: Fire inspectors and local firehouse companies walk through businesses unannounced and answer 311 complaints. They check extinguisher tags, exit paths, extension cords and permits, then write a violation order to fix it or a summons to the city tribunal (OATH), where the fine is halved if you prove the fix before the hearing.

officials.name: Buildings inspector
officials.realProcess: Almost always sent by a 311 complaint: a neighbor hears demolition or sees a dumpster and no permit in the window. The inspector posts a Stop Work Order and writes a summons to OATH. The work must be legalized with filed plans before the order is lifted.

officials.name: Sanitation enforcement agent
officials.realProcess: Agents walk commercial streets on a route. For dirty sidewalks they may ticket a shop only during two posted one-hour windows a day; for trash set out wrong, missing carter decals and sidewalk obstructions they ticket at any time. Tickets are answered at OATH.

officials.name: Environmental inspector
officials.realProcess: Three separate units: sewer inspectors open the grease interceptor and ask for cleaning records; the cross-connection unit mails a notice when the yearly backflow test report is missing; noise inspectors answer 311 complaints and take a decibel reading inside the neighbor's home.
